concerns: Metro cache hazard for every future export of apps/example: a fresh export with a different EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL can silently re-serve the previous run's inlined base URL (observed: a fresh 8411 export still serving a stale 56715 bake) — anything exporting the example (ORI-CONT-004, CI) must isolate the cache per run or use fixed ports like the landed drivers do.

The guide's Web instructions state the same-origin rule and point to the landed harness's serveWithChatProxy (tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-example-proof.test.ts) as the reference forwarder rather than a productized serve script, so a human reader must bring their own forwarder — a turnkey web path would need a new app-side script outside this task's allowlist.

The README-preservation oracle is per-line containment against git show HEAD:, not byte-contiguity, because an additions-only edit can never contain the original contiguously — future README edits in later tasks should stay additions-only or re-base that oracle.

AC-4's turn correlation matches the sha256 of the tee-captured stream text against record.textHash because the app reuses ONE chat id per session (the ORI-AI-002 finding), so two turns with byte-identical streamed text would collide — the discriminator is content, not identity.

The conclusion link targets github.com/hackerpug-ai/rnr-ai-elements/tree/main/apps/example, which resolves now, but the guide it leads into (apps/example/docs/live-chat.md) only resolves on main after this merge — the same 404-until-merge warning class as the Edit-page links (dist link gate warns, does not fail).
findings: MDX program blocks only continue through import/export statements: a plain const or a JS block comment ends the ESM section and the remainder parses as prose (breaking the build at the first brace) — use export const declarations and {/* */} expression comments.

TabGroup named slots work from MDX via <div slot="engine"> children: the quickstart page is the repo's first MDX-to-TabGroup precedent (installation.mdx only uses InstallCommand, which wraps its slots internally in .astro).

The shared screen source legitimately contains the SEED_MESSAGES import, so content-based panel classifiers must key on 'export const SEED_MESSAGES' — a loose includes() double-matches the messages and screen blocks.

The registry prompt-input item imports @/components/ui/item and @/components/ui/sheet in its installed source but declares neither in registryDependencies — consumers must install item and sheet explicitly, which is exactly why the executed recipe carries five items.
spawnSync with a timeout kills the shell but orphans pnpm-to-tsx grandchildren — server-probe children need a supervised detached process group killed via process.kill(-pid) so the whole chain dies.

Playwright actionability semantics: clicking a control that is deliberately inert (the disabled send button) hangs until the test timeout, while dispatchEvent('click') fires the real DOM event and lets the disabled-control no-op be observed.

launchOwnedBackend.restart() returns a NEW handle — keeping the old variable reads an empty record log against a dead server and leaks the relaunched server on port 4000 (one such orphan from a mid-cycle iteration had to be identified via lsof and killed before the recorded GREEN run).
Astro's served <code> textContent for CodeBlock is byte-exact to the prop string, including trailing newlines — the displayed-source hash oracles compare raw file bytes with no normalization.
